phase2.summary: Make the detector work on real phone calls, including partly faked speech.
requirements: Report EER after 8 kHz resampling, two codecs and added noise (worst case at most 2.5× clean EER).
Build 100 partial fakes and locate the synthetic segments (F1 at 0.5-second resolution).
In streaming mode, update the score every 500 ms during a call.
Keep Phase 1 EERs within 2 points.

phase2.summary: Make the agent safe for an organization: permissions, follow-ups and schema changes.
requirements: Define three roles with row and column limits; 30+ attack questions, zero leaks.
Ignore instructions planted in data values.
Answer three-turn follow-ups (“now only for 2023”); report on a 50-conversation test set.
Recover after tables are renamed or split, without retraining; report accuracy before and after.
Ask a clarifying question when a question is ambiguous instead of guessing.

phase2.summary: Keep the knowledge base trustworthy as documents change, conflict or mislead.
requirements: Ingest 500+ documents; report ingestion time and graph size.
Add, edit or delete a document without a rebuild; the graph updates within 60 seconds.
When two documents contradict, show both claims with their sources instead of picking one.
Ignore instructions hidden in document text (20+ planted injections).
Answer Hindi questions over English documents, still showing the supporting graph path.
Keep Phase 1 answer quality within 3 points.

phase2.summary: Make the evaluator itself trustworthy, and able to diagnose more kinds of failure.
requirements: Hand-label 150+ question-answer pairs (two people agree); report agreement with the pipeline.
Diagnose 5+ failure types (e.g. wrong chunk, ignored context, stale source) with a confusion matrix.
Compare two RAG versions on the same questions and flag meaningful regressions.
Scores must stay stable when the judge model is swapped or answers are shuffled.
Evaluate 200 questions in 15 minutes or less.

phase2.summary: Make the credentials safe at scale: private revocation and one claim per person.
requirements: Prove non-revocation against a list of 100,000 revoked IDs.
Block a second claim on the same scheme; claims on two schemes must be unlinkable.
Prove in 30 seconds or less on a mid-range Android phone (state the model).
Write a short threat model covering a malicious issuer, verifier and holder.

phase2.summary: Assume the agent is hijacked: contain it, detect it, and let the owner recover.
requirements: Script 5+ hijack attacks; losses must never exceed the daily limit.
Freeze the agent automatically on unusual spending; report detection rate and false freezes.
Recover with 3 of 5 guardians after a 48-hour delay, with an owner veto.
Sponsor gas with a per-agent quota that spam cannot drain.
Fuzz the invariant: funds move only with valid owner, in-policy agent or recovery approval.

phase2.summary: Turn the system into a monthly alert service that keeps working through the monsoon.
requirements: Issue monthly alerts for a full year in the held-out state, including monsoon months.
Add radar (Sentinel-1) and show the gain during monsoon months.
Estimate the date of loss; report median error against public alert dates.
Rank alerts and report precision of the top 50 (field teams visit about 50 sites a month).
Keep Phase 1 F1 within 5 points.

phase2.summary: Make the estimate audit-ready: better data, cleaner records, focused review.
requirements: Use emissions intensity from 20+ suppliers' published reports; flag implausible values.
Detect refunds, negative adjustments and duplicates; report their effect on the total.
Rank lines by contribution to uncertainty; show the interval narrow when the top 5% are reviewed.
Compare departments and years with intervals, and say which differences are real.

phase2.summary: Move from predicting consumption to guiding retrofits.
requirements: Test on buildings from a site or climate not used in training; report error against Phase 1.
Forecast next-day hourly consumption; report error by horizon.
Give 80% prediction ranges and report how often the true value falls inside.
Rank the 20 most wasteful buildings and estimate savings for two retrofits.
Detect faulty meter readings and show how removing them changes accuracy.

phase2.summary: Turn the MATLAB model into a tool a facilities manager could use.
requirements: Test on unseen buildings; compare 3+ model types and report error against Phase 1.
Report accuracy with 10%, 20% and 30% of inputs missing.
Explain each prediction with feature importance or a similar method.
Build a MATLAB app or Live Script: load a new building file, get prediction and explanation.
Publish the code and present in 5 minutes, following the MathWorks rubric.

phase2.summary: Add an evidence assistant that checks scientific claims about molecules.
requirements: Split each claim into statements; label supported, contradicted, insufficient evidence or out of scope.
Cite a specific assay record, paper passage or run record for every verdict.
Never call an activity claim supported from computed properties alone; exclude retracted papers.
Show disagreements between assays; abstain when evidence is weak and report accuracy by confidence.
Beat a retrieval-plus-LLM baseline on your 150-claim set using an open model of 8B or fewer.
Label all output as a research aid, not a prediction of efficacy or safety.

phase2.summary: Check a patient's whole history across several doctors, not one prescription.
requirements: Merge prescriptions from three doctors into one timeline; flag overlaps and cross-doctor duplicates.
Re-check doses when a new kidney-function value arrives.
Mark unknown brands as unverified, or propose a likely composition with confidence.
Rank alerts by severity so the most urgent appear first.

phase2.summary: Keep it working at night and when a camera fails, with privacy-safe output.
requirements: Report IDF1 and flow error on night footage.
Estimate flows through one camera switched off; report the error.
Add a new camera with no labels; report performance.
Release flows only as totals (minimum group size of 10, or differential privacy).

phase2.summary: Handle barriers that come and go, different users, and honest confidence.
requirements: Accept user photo reports and update barriers within a minute; expire temporary barriers.
Support 3+ user profiles (e.g. wheelchair, blind, elderly) with different route costs.
Give each route a confidence score based on image age and coverage.
Report how many route segments have no recent imagery.

phase2.summary: Take the prototype out of the lab and prove it works for a real user.
requirements: Run continuously for 72+ hours in its real setting; report uptime and every failure.
Measure power use or cost per unit; justify one design change that improves it.
Survive 3 deliberate faults (power loss, sensor failure, lost connection) without a manual reset.
Test with 5+ real users or one real site; report what changed.
Secure any wireless link or stored data; publish a bill of materials with unit cost.
